coverage: Monday 17 August, complete in both Asia and the US. Written 08:45 SGT, after Tuesday's Asia open — so today's HK and SGX marks are NOT in here. Xiaomi's H1 results land TONIGHT after the HK close. First edition produced on the new architecture: prices and the release calendar were fetched deterministically in code before any agent ran, so this took 6 agents instead of the 42 Sunday's catch-up needed.
tldr: GOLD FINALLY HELD A BREAKOUT. New high 4,486.50, closed 4,479.50 (+2.26%) within $7 of it — after three consecutive failed attempts on 12-14 Aug. What makes it credible is the backdrop: it did this WHILE the 30Y sat above 5.2%, its highest since 2007, which normally kills gold. So the engine is debasement and haven demand, not falling real rates. More durable than a rate-cut trade — but it unwinds fast if US-Iran talks resume.

OIL BROKE OUT ON A REAL, DATED CATALYST: Brent 91.11 (+2.93%), clear of the range top. The June US-Iran MOU formally EXPIRED Monday, Trump declined to extend, and a senior Iranian official told Reuters Tehran must prepare to escalate in Hormuz, with a several-week ultimatum. One caution the verification forced: a widely-circulated story about vessel transits collapsing was DELETED — independent maritime tracking showed 12 transits on 16 Aug. This is a diplomatic escalation, not a confirmed supply outage.

THE CONTRADICTION SITTING UNDER YOUR BOOK: that same oil move is the named driver behind the long end and the September hike tail — which is the direct threat to 1.6x levered silver. Your oil sleeve and your metals sleeve are now hedging each other by accident rather than design.

SILVER IS STILL THE WEAKER HALF. Its best close of the run at 66.065 (+1.66%, about +2.66% levered), but its 66.145 high is STILL below the 66.650 high of 12 Aug — a lower high. And there is no silver-specific driver anywhere in the dated commentary: no squeeze, no inventory event. The gold/silver ratio widened to 67.8, meaning silver underperformed gold on a strong day for both. The level that matters is 66.65.

CHECK YOUR OCBC LINE — the headline is wrong. It shows -0.76%, but it went ex 47 cents Monday. Against the ex-adjusted 31.32 reference it actually ROSE 0.73%. If your P&L marks it to 31.55 without accruing the receivable, the book understates it by ~1.5% until 28 August and shows a loss on a day the bank gained. Same trap ran on DBS Friday: that -1.07% was the S$0.81 dividend almost exactly.

CHINA MISSED ON ALL FOUR MEASURES — industrial production 4.5%, retail sales 0.6%, fixed-asset investment -6.7% (lowest since April 2020), unemployment 5.2% — with the data in hand an HOUR before the HK close. Hong Kong rallied 1.34% anyway, snapping four straight losses. Semiconductors set the tape, not macro. That is good for SMIC and Xiaomi and a bad reason to own China breadth.

XIAOMI REPORTS TONIGHT, after the HK close, with the investor call at 19:30 Beijing. Your 26,662 shares trade blind through today's session and the gap risk is Wednesday's open. The filing says an interim dividend is 'if any' — a dividend alongside a sharp profit decline would be the genuine surprise.

SMIC is still the one that is working: +6.14% to HK$75.15 on Q2 gross margin of 25.3% against 20-22% guided, with Q3 guided up another 1-3pp on wafers ALREADY contracted at higher prices. Correction to what we said: Monday was the SECOND post-results session, not the third — so this is earlier in the move than it looked.

signals: The most useful fact of the day is a contradiction: gold made a new high while the long end sat at post-2007 highs. Those two things do not normally coexist. It means the bid is monetary — debasement, haven, central-bank buying — rather than a rate-cut trade. Watch whether it survives contact with the FOMC minutes on Thursday.

Your oil and metals sleeves are now negatively correlated through the Fed. The Hormuz escalation lifts crude, crude lifts the inflation impulse, the impulse lifts the long end and the hike tail, and that is exactly what hurts 1.6x levered silver. A resolution in the Strait would reverse all four legs at once. That is concentration risk wearing a diversification costume.

Silver has now failed at 66.65 twice and has no story of its own. Every dated piece of commentary attributes its move to macro. Until it clears that level on a silver-specific catalyst, treat it as a high-beta gold proxy carrying leverage — which is the least attractive way to own the trade.

The K-shape printed twice on the same day: Singapore's electronics exports +112% while non-electronics FELL 2.3%; China's high-tech output booming while retail sales grew 0.6% and investment contracted 6.7%. The AI hardware cycle is now demonstrably decoupled from the economies hosting it — which is why HK could rally through a four-way macro miss.

Empire State's four-year high is stagflationary underneath: new orders and shipments fell, the strength came from constraint, prices paid accelerated and prices received FELL. Margin compression at the firm level is the mechanism that eventually reaches equities, and it corroborates both the gold breakout and the long end's refusal to rally.
